blocks.text: But, they ask, why do Job and David attribute this demand for food not to the ravens themselves, but to the chicks of the ravens? [col. 205] To answer this question the Hebrews and Arabs devise many things, as will be clear from what follows. Rabbi Eliezer in the Capitula, near the end of ch. 21: When the ravens have hatched their chicks and see that they are white, they flee from them, thinking that they are the young of a serpent; then God, the Holy One, Blessed be He, grants them food without want. R. Selomo on Job: יתעו מבלי אכל שאביהם שונאם והקב״ה מזמן להם יתושים הנבראים מצואתן ונכנסין לתוך פיהם, They wander without food, because they are hateful to their father; but God, the Holy One, Blessed be He, prepares for them gnats, generated from their own dung, which enter into their mouth. Aben Ezra on Psalm CXLVII.: חכמי הגויים אומרים כי אבותם יעזבום בהולדם, The philosophers of the gentiles assert that they are deserted by their parents as soon as they are born. And Kimchi: לפי שהם לבנים בהולדם ואמותיהם מניחים אותם ולא יביאו להם טרפם כי יחשבו כי אינם בניהם לפי שהם לבנים והם צווחים כאלו יקראו לאל בעד טרפם והקב״ה מזמין להם יתושין ואוכלים אותם, because they are born white, their mothers desert them and do not bring them food; for they do not recognize them as their own, since they are white. Therefore they cry out, as if they were asking God for their food. And God prepares gnats for them to feed on. So much for the Hebrews; now hear the Arabs. Among them the poet Hariri sings thus in مقامة [maqāma] Mekama, or stantia, 13.
يا رازق النعاب في عشه [yā rāziq al-naʿʿāb fī ʿushshihi] وجابر العظم الكسير المهيض [wa-jābir al-ʿaẓm al-kasīr al-mahīḍ]
